title: ChromoMapperWeb: evaluate genome alignments and track assembly steps within an interactive graphic environment.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Fetched the live tool homepage (HTTP 200, no login, uploads kept 48 h) and read its text and every link it offers: the only links are 'try sample data' and 'help', both inside the session-based web app. Downloaded and unpacked the complete Europe PMC supplementary archive (2.43 MB): it contains one PDF of supplementary text/figures and 12 figure images, zero data tables. Read the data availability statement, methods and full text; searched the full text for 'github', 'download', 'zenodo', 'figshare', 'example data', 'source code' and found no dataset link at all.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The identity of the ~11 genome assemblies used as worked examples (GCF_000013425.1 Staphylococcus aureus reference, GCA_011064465.1/.2 two versions of one human individual genome, six haplotype-phased human cell-line assemblies GCA_040939325.1/GCA_040939355.1/GCA_021951015.1/GCA_021950905.1/GCA_050656345.1/GCA_050656315.1, plus the human T2T reference GCF_009914755.1) and the Salzberg et al. bacterial assemblies. I did not download any of these genome FASTA files; their sizes and contents are from the paper and from general knowledge of NCBI assemblies, not verified here.

a1_downloadable.note: The web tool is live and needs no login, but the paper deposits no dataset of any kind: no repository accession for its own data, no supplementary tables, no GitHub, no Zenodo data record (the Zenodo entry found is the companion command-line tool's source code, not data). The only 'data' are pointers to ~11 third-party NCBI genome assemblies, and the alignment outputs the paper actually analyses were never released. Verified by unpacking the full supplement and scanning the whole text.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Decisive failure. There is no table and therefore no label column anywhere. To get a prediction target (for example 'this alignment block marks a misassembly') you would have to download multi-gigabyte genomes, run nucmer or QUAST yourself, and then hand-curate which discontinuities are real errors versus true biological differences. That is constructing the label from scratch, which is exactly the A2 fail condition.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are referenced, not present: eight to eleven NCBI accession numbers rather than files. The actual model inputs would be nucmer/QUAST alignment blocks that do not exist publicly and would have to be regenerated.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessable; stopped at A2. No measurement table exists, so there is nothing to carry units.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not assessable; stopped at A2. No labelled rows exist. The unit of analysis closest to a sample would be the genome assembly, and there are about eleven of those.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~8-10 GB of compressed human genome FASTA plus whole-genome nucmer alignments
a6_fits_laptop.note: Generating the inputs means whole-genome alignment of eight human haplotype assemblies against the T2T reference. That is far beyond a 16 GB CPU-only laptop in any reasonable wall-clock time, and the files breach the 50 MB download rule many times over. Estimated, not timed.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not assessable; stopped at A2. There are no counts to compare because nothing was deposited.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable; stopped at A2. No label exists. Any label would come from the authors' own visual interpretation of alignment plots, which is subjective annotation rather than a physical measurement.

existing_models.name: ResMiCo (residual neural network for identifying misassembled contigs)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported by its authors as substantially more accurate than prior tools at reference-free misassembly detection, with robustness checks on novel taxonomic diversity and different assemblers; exact numbers not retrieved beyond the abstract.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalisation to taxa and assembly methods not seen in training is the part they stress-test and flag.

existing_models.name: DeepMM (deep learning identification and correction of metagenome misassemblies)
existing_models.score_and_split: Authors report raising near-complete metagenome-assembled genomes from 905 to 1006 in a real metagenomic dataset after correction; from the abstract only.

existing_models.name: metaMIC (reference-free misassembly identification and correction)
existing_models.score_and_split: Identifies misassembled contigs and localises breakpoints in de novo metagenomic assemblies; numbers not retrieved.

existing_models.name: AutoHiC (deep learning correction of chromosome-level assemblies from Hi-C contact maps)
existing_models.score_and_split: Published in Nucleic Acids Research 2024 as an automated replacement for manual Hi-C curation; numbers not retrieved.

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: No join is possible because the paper contributes no records to join.

controls.positive_control: none available - no data to run one on

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper contributes a drawing program for alignment files, not a dataset, so nothing here can be trained on or tested.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use genome alignment block patterns to predict which assembly regions are genuine errors rather than real biological differences.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show a model the geometry of alignment blocks between a draft genome assembly and a trusted reference: block positions, lengths, orientations, gaps and overlaps. The number of labelled examples available from this paper is zero; it describes roughly eleven genome assemblies and releases none of the derived alignment tables.
plain_idea.predict: A yes/no call per region on whether a break in alignment is an assembly mistake. The true answer would have to come from expert manual curation of assembly plots, or from a simulated genome where errors were injected on purpose - neither exists in this paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Genome assembly curation is still largely done by eye, so automating it would save real time for sequencing consortia. But that case has to be made on someone else's data, because this paper supplies none, and four deep-learning tools already attack it.

more_or_better_data.why: We would have no data at all. ResMiCo, DeepMM and metaMIC were each trained on large simulated or real metagenomic assembly collections; this paper releases zero labelled regions.

confidence_score.why: Calibrated per-prediction confidence needs replicate or repeated measurements of the same quantity. Nothing is measured here; the tool draws rectangles from alignment coordinates.

models_beatable.why: ResMiCo (PLOS Computational Biology) and AutoHiC (Nucleic Acids Research 2024) are recent neural networks whose authors already ran cross-assembler and cross-taxon generalisation checks, and DeepMM is a 2025 preprint. There is no stale baseline to pick off.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Every condition fails: we have no training data, no shared evaluation split with any of these tools, and no join key linking this paper to anything they used.

ml_idea: The only idea this paper suggests - classify alignment discontinuities as assembly errors versus true biological variation - cannot be started from this paper, because it publishes no alignment tables, no labels and no code for the web tool. Anyone wanting to do it should begin from ResMiCo's or metaMIC's released training sets instead.

effort.compute_note: No estimate is meaningful because there is no dataset. Building one from the eleven cited NCBI assemblies would require whole-genome nucmer alignments of human-scale genomes, which is a server job, not a laptop job; this is an estimate, nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the supplementary archive and list its contents. It holds one PDF and twelve figure images and no data table - two minutes of work that kills the project outright.

verdict_reason: This is a web-based visualisation tool, not a dataset. It fails A1 in substance (nothing deposited: the supplement is a PDF plus figures, there is no repository record, no GitHub, and the Zenodo entry found is the companion command-line tool's source code) and fails A2 outright (no table, no label column, and any prediction target would have to be built from scratch by regenerating multi-gigabyte whole-genome alignments and hand-curating them). The nearest real task, automated misassembly detection, is already served by at least four deep-learning tools (ResMiCo, DeepMM, metaMIC, AutoHiC), and we would enter it with no data of our own.
